artists.biography: A Formal Horse is a new progressive rock quartet based in Southampton. Although the band's sound is difficult to pinpoint, their dense instrumental passages are reminiscent of King Crimson and Mahavishnu Orchestra, whilst Francesca Lewis' lead vocals evoke the whimsical surrealism of the 1970s Canterbury scene. However, A Formal Horse go beyond simply regurgitating the music of their predecessors. With influences as diverse as Bartok and Bon Iver, the band prove that there is still much territory to be explored in the field of British progressive rock.They have recently recorded their debut EP with Rob Aubrey (IQ, Big Big Train). Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Here Comes a Man from the Council with a Flamethrower" is the debut album by Southampton-based rock quartet A Formal Horse, originally released in 2018 on the Plane Groovy label. The album is characterized by its quirky, song-based approach to progressive rock, blending angular rhythms, off-kilter melodies, and a distinct sense of "violent whimsy." Drawing from art rock and avant-garde influences, the music features intricate arrangements, sharp lyrical wit, and a dynamic interplay between aggression and playfulness, establishing the band's unique identity within the modern prog scene.

As A Formal Horse's first full-length release, "Here Comes a Man from the Council with a Flamethrower" set the stage for their subsequent work, including their 2021 follow-up "Meat Mallet." The album received positive attention from progressive rock enthusiasts and critics for its originality and fearless experimentation, helping to cement the band's reputation as a distinctive voice in the genre. While not a mainstream commercial success, it found a dedicated audience among fans of adventurous rock music and remains a notable entry in the Plane Groovy catalog.
